question: Which of the following dances developed in the monasteries of Assam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form that originated in the **monasteries of Assam**.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardeva** in the 15th century as a medium for religious expression and storytelling.
 
• The dance form is an integral part of the **Sattras (monastic institutions)** and was traditionally performed by male monks known as **Bhakats**.
 
• **Sattriya** dance includes various elements such as **nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), and natya (dramatic elements)**.
 
• In 2000, **Sattriya** was recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya** dance is characterized by its use of **hand gestures (mudras), footwork (padas), and facial expressions (abhinaya)**.
 
• The costumes typically include traditional Assamese attire with elaborate jewelry and headgear.
 
• Music accompanying **Sattriya** dance is based on classical ragas and is performed using traditional instruments like the **khol (drum), taals (cymbals), and flute**.
 
• Over time, **Sattriya** has evolved and is now performed by both men and women on various cultural platforms.
